title: Regression sentinel for function-call selection and argument fidelity
creator: Jared Kim
description:
Problem statement:
We have seen intermittent regressions in downstream tool/function calling correctness after model swaps and config changes (quantization profile, batching changes, and policy routing). Existing evals focus on call rate and high-level success metrics but do not reliably detect subtle selection shifts (e.g., choosing secondary fallback tools instead of primary) or argument corruption (truncated/reshuffled args, type mismatches).

Goal:
Build a lightweight, continuous 'regression sentinel' that runs after any model or config change and flags deviations in: tool selection accuracy, argument schema validity, and argument content fidelity. The sentinel should tie regressions to the change that triggered them, produce actionable diffs, and integrate with existing alerting and rollout gates so we can block rollouts with high-confidence regressions.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: automated post-deploy evals for hosted/runtime config changes, model version rollouts, and quantization profile switches; selection accuracy, argument validation, and delta reporting; alerting to SRE/Release engineers and gating rollouts in console.
- Out of scope: building a user-facing UI for triage (we will link to existing dashboards), exhaustive semantic correctness checks for arbitrary tool outputs (only argument-level fidelity and selection will be measured).
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel runs automatically after any model or runtime-config change and within the rollout pipeline for canary deploys.
Detects changes in tool selection distribution with configurable thresholds (baseline vs new) and reports per-tool precision/recall style metrics.
Validates argument shapes and types against registered tool schemas and flags schema failures and content anomalies (e.g., missing required fields, truncated strings, base64 corruption).
Produces a compact regression report that includes: before/after selection histograms, top N argument diffs with examples, and a suggested severity score.
Integrates with alerting: sends to #runtime-regressions Slack channel and opens PagerDuty only for high-severity incidents.
Can be configured to block a rollout when severity exceeds configured threshold, and exposes an override reason logged to the rollout trace.
Has unit and integration tests covering injected model/config changes and synthetic failure modes (selection flip, arg truncation, type mismatch).
plan: Design sentinel pipeline and data schema in Confluence (links below).
Implement offline evaluator that loads pre- and post-change request traces, computes selection/arg fidelity metrics, and generates report JSON.
Add lightweight instrumentation to the runtime to tag traces with config/model revision IDs and export example request-response pairs to the evaluator sink.
Wire the evaluator into the deployment pipeline: run after canary step and before promote-to-prod; add gating checks in rollout manager.
Hook alerting to existing runtime incident channels and create a dedicated runbook for triage.
Ship tests and document expected thresholds for P0/P1/P2 severities.
metrics: Selection accuracy delta (top-1 distribution KL divergence and per-tool drop in selection rate).
Argument schema failure rate (percent of calls with invalid/malformed args).
Argument content corruption rate (heuristics: truncation, unexpected nulls, base64 invalid).
False-positive rate (measured via periodic synthetic golden runs).
Time-to-detect (median minutes from deploy to alert).
notifications: Rollout manager: block/promote flag with link to report JSON.
Ticketing: auto-open ENG ticket when severity & regression score above threshold.
